pr.title: Avoid ICE in coverage builds with bad `#[coverage(..)]` attributes
pr.description:
This code can sometimes witness malformed coverage attributes in builds that are going to fail, so use `span_delayed_bug` to avoid an inappropriate ICE in that case.

Fixes #127880.
pr.author: Zalathar

analysis.originalLogic: `coverage_attr_on` inspects a def's `#[coverage(..)]` attributes: `Some([item]) if item.has_name(sym::on) => return true,` and the other parsed forms fall through. For the shape it considered impossible it used the comment `// Other possibilities should have been rejected by `rustc_parse::validate_attr`.` and then aborted with `tcx.dcx().span_bug(attr.span, "unexpected value of coverage attribute");`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: For the malformed/unexpected `#[coverage(..)]` case, the fallback branch reports via the aborting `tcx.dcx().span_bug(attr.span, "unexpected value of coverage attribute");` rather than a non-aborting delayed bug. Consequently an already-failing coverage build panics with `error: internal compiler error: unexpected value of coverage attribute` instead of merely recording the unexpected value and continuing to report ordinary diagnostics. The fix changes that call to `tcx.dcx().span_delayed_bug(attr.span, "unexpected value of coverage attribute");` with the note `// Use `span_delayed_bug` to avoid an ICE in failing builds (#127880).`
analysis.inputDomain: Rust source compiled with coverage instrumentation (`-Cinstrument-coverage`) that contains a malformed `#[coverage(..)]` attribute, e.g. bare `#[coverage]` on a function such as `#[coverage]` followed by `fn main() {}`, with or without the `coverage_attribute` feature enabled. The malformed attribute is expected to be rejected by `rustc_parse::validate_attr`, but `coverage_attr_on` can still be queried during MIR building/analysis in the failing build.
analysis.summary: Bug fix in the InstrumentCoverage query `coverage_attr_on`: malformed `#[coverage(..)]` attributes can still reach this query in builds that are already failing validation, so the unexpected-value branch must use `span_delayed_bug` instead of aborting `span_bug` to avoid an ICE. Regression coverage moved from a `tests/crashes` known-bug test to a revisioned UI test.
analysis.trigger: `coverage_attr_on` encounters a `coverage` attribute whose parsed argument shape is neither exactly `on` nor the accepted off-form (for example `#[coverage]`), and this query is reached while compiling with coverage instrumentation (e.g. during `mir_built`/analysis), even though the crate is going to fail due to the malformed attribute or its feature gate.
preconditions: Include a malformed `#[coverage]` attribute (the reported reproducer is a bare `#[coverage]` followed by `fn main() {}`).
The malformed attribute reaches `coverage_attr_on` despite `rustc_parse::validate_attr` being expected to reject it, because the build is already failing.
Test both `coverage_attribute` feature-enabled and feature-disabled revisions, since the disabled case additionally emits the E0658 feature-gate error.
pitfalls: Do not assume `rustc_parse::validate_attr` always prevents malformed coverage attributes from reaching MIR/query code; failing builds can still invoke `coverage_attr_on`.

`span_delayed_bug` does not make the program compile successfully: the malformed attribute must still be reported (e.g. `error: malformed `coverage` attribute input`), and with the feature disabled `error[E0658]: the `#[coverage]` attribute is an experimental feature` also appears. Assert absence of the ICE/panic, not successful compilation.
The new delayed-bug message may be emitted alongside normal validation errors; judge success by no `internal compiler error`/panic, not by only one diagnostic.
Removal of `tests/crashes/127880.rs` is not loss of regression coverage; the case was moved into `tests/ui/coverage-attr/bad-attr-ice.rs`.
Coverage UI tests need profiler support (`//@ needs-profiler-support`) because they use `-Cinstrument-coverage`.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a UI regression test `tests/ui/coverage-attr/bad-attr-ice.rs` with `//@ revisions: feat nofeat`, `//@ compile-flags: -Cinstrument-coverage`, and `//@ needs-profiler-support`; use `#![cfg_attr(feat, feature(coverage_attribute))]` and the minimal program consisting of a bare `#[coverage]` attribute followed by `fn main() {}`. Check the `feat` stderr for `error: malformed `coverage` attribute input` and the `nofeat` stderr additionally for `error[E0658]: the `#[coverage]` attribute is an experimental feature`, and verify neither output contains `internal compiler error` or the `unexpected value of coverage attribute` panic. This replaces the prior `tests/crashes/127880.rs` known-bug test.
evidence: // Use `span_delayed_bug` to avoid an ICE in failing builds (#127880).
// Other possibilities should have been rejected by `rustc_parse::validate_attr`.
